VIEWFINITY / COLOR LAB / EDUCATION

Understand Colors.

COLOR IS MORE THAN A HEX CODE.AN EXPLORATION OF MEANING, HISTORY & PURPOSE

Every color tells a story. Learn its visual associations, cultural histories, color-wheel roles, and the kind of message it can bring to your next project.

Color meanings are not universal laws. They depend on people, culture, context, contrast, and the other colors around them.

THE FOUNDATION / 01

What makes a color primary?

01 / TRADITIONAL PAINT

RYB

Red, yellow and blue are the traditional primaries used in introductory art and pigment mixing. Orange, green and violet are called secondary colors in this system.

02 / DIGITAL LIGHT

RGB

Red, green and blue are the additive primaries of screens. Combining them as light creates other displayed colors, and full intensity produces white.

03 / INK & PRINT

CMYK

Cyan, magenta and yellow are subtractive process primaries; black is added for richer darks and practical printing. A color’s category therefore depends on the color system.

THE COLOR ENCYCLOPEDIA / 02

Choose a color. Learn its story.

16 COLORS TO EXPLORE

Context changes everything.

Research finds recurring links between colors and emotions, but those links are many-to-many rather than fixed. Before deciding what a color means, examine the audience, surrounding imagery, saturation, brightness, cultural context and contrast.
